cards.title: Brute Force
cards.description_long: Brute force attacks attempt to guess passwords by systematically trying all possible combinations until the correct one is found. Attackers often automate this process using scripts or specialized tools.

main_commands.explanation: Attempt login using a password list
Try multiple usernames and passwords against SSH
Perform brute force attack on SSH service
Crack password hashes using a wordlist

activity: Attempt password guessing using a wordlist
Test brute force against a login form
Understand difference between online and offline brute force
Observe how account lockout policies stop brute force
Analyze password strength against brute force attempts

cards.title: Password Spraying
cards.description_short: Try common passwords on many accounts
cards.description_long: Password spraying attacks try a small number of common passwords across many user accounts. This avoids account lockouts that occur when too many attempts are made on a single account.

main_commands.explanation: Try a single common password across many accounts

activity: Test common passwords across multiple accounts
Observe how spraying avoids account lockouts
Analyze common weak passwords
Practice detection of spraying attempts in logs
Understand mitigation using MFA and password policies

cards.title: Session Hijacking
cards.description_short: Take over a valid user session
cards.description_long: Session hijacking occurs when an attacker steals or predicts a valid session ID to impersonate a user. This allows the attacker to access the system without needing the actual password.
activity: Inspect session cookies in a browser
Use proxy tools to capture HTTP requests
Analyze session tokens in intercepted traffic
Understand risks of unencrypted HTTP sessions
Learn how secure cookies and HTTPS mitigate hijacking

cards.title: Credential Stuffing
cards.description_short: Use leaked credentials to access accounts
cards.description_long: Credential stuffing uses previously leaked username-password combinations from data breaches to attempt logins on other websites. Since many users reuse passwords, attackers often gain unauthorized access.

main_commands.explanation: Load credential combos into testing tool

activity: Test login attempts using leaked credential lists
Analyze how password reuse increases risk
Observe automated login request patterns
Practice detection using login monitoring
Understand protections like MFA and rate limiting
